title: Complex Parsing for In-Network Acceleration of High-Energy Physics Experiments
problem: High-Energy Physics (HEP) experiments like DUNE generate massive volumes of network traffic with custom packet formats. Processing this data at the compute layer creates bottlenecks. In-network processing on programmable switches could offload parsing.
motivation: DUNE experiment produces Jumbo Ethernet frames containing digitized sensor readings. Current approaches process data entirely at compute nodes. Programmable networking hardware (Tofino switches) offers opportunity for early-stage packet filtering and parsing.
method: The approach builds a parser—a tool that breaks down data into usable pieces—for DUNE's custom packet format directly into a Tofino programmable network switch, which is reconfigurable hardware in the network itself. Rather than sending all raw data to computers for processing, the switch performs the parsing as packets flow through the network. The team tested this setup using real network traffic from the ICEBERG DUNE prototype detector on the FABRIC testbed, measuring the switch's processing speed and identifying performance bottlenecks.
key_novelty: This shows that programmable network switches can handle parsing High-Energy Physics experiment data directly, instead of relying on computers to do it after the data arrives.
contributions: Custom packet parser implementation for DUNE protocol on Tofino switch
Evaluation on FABRIC testbed with ICEBERG DUNE prototype traffic
Identification of parser implementation challenges for custom HEP formats
Performance bottleneck analysis and mitigation strategies
Early investigation of programmable networking for HEP data reduction
limitations: Early-stage investigation; no speedup/throughput metrics provided. Limited to DUNE protocol; generalization to other HEP experiments unclear. Scalability to full DUNE detector not evaluated. Resource constraints (switch memory/processing) not fully explored.
